paragraphs.source_en: During the next two hundred years, the arguments of Leibniz and others against assigning space an independent reality generated hardly an echo in the scientific community. 9 Instead, the pendulum had clearly swung to Newton's view of space; his laws of motion, founded on his con cept of absolute space, took center stage. Certainly, the success of these laws in describing observations was the essential reason for their acceptance. It's striking to note, however, that Newton himself viewed all of his achievements in physics as merely forming the solid foundation to sup port what he considered his really important discovery: absolute space. For Newton, it was all about space. 10
